description:
This tragic science-fiction love story is a social satire that calls attention to modern issues of cloning, human trafficking, and our desire for eternal life.

Feast your eyes on this visual masterpiece defined by its unique pastel-like colors and textures. Enter the mind of artist and writer Indigo/Canned Story and explore the philosophical meaning behind human nature and existence. She introduces a disturbing futuristic world where corporations conduct experiments to extend human life. Out of 50 human subjects that participate in the 'Eternal Life Project,' only one survives. Seul, also referred to the "Goddess," obtains eternal life, but at the cost of losing all her emotions.

"She can only remember living. But she cannot feel it." - Episode 5: Goddess

Diagnosed with terminal illness, 'Eternal Life Project' was Seul's sole option to wait for her lover, Ohn, who promised that he would return for her. Living as a doll, 50 years passed in waiting.

Despite losing her emotions, one can argue that Seul's love, arguably the most powerful of human emotions, still remained. Or perhaps, Indigo/Canned Story is showing that love is often mistaken for fading memories that humans hold on to.

"I don't want to forget you. Not even the tiniest, most insignificant things about you. Your eyes. The shape of your lips. Not even the softest sighs that escape from your mouth." - Episode 1: Prologue

Salty Rain is an instant classic that is meant to be read and reread. With every read, you will discover new details in both art and story.
